subject: Audit stream sanitization: discovery recap & POC request

Subject: Audit stream sanitization: discovery recap & POC request

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track requirements and the POC ask.

Call highlights (short):
- Scope: request/response audit stream, request and response bodies, headers, and tracing metadata (trace IDs/span ids).
- Primary asks: ensure no PHI/sysid/SSN in logs; demonstrate an approach to keep observability for debugging while removing/replacing sensitive values; support US-only residency for logs.
- Constraints: Acme wants a 90-day retention default but can accept shorter retained raw data; all stored logs must be encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS).

Open questions we need clarified from Acme before POC: 
1) Which header fields should be considered sensitive by default? (we heard Authorization, Cookie, X-Forwarded-For; please add others)
2) Are trace IDs allowed as-is for correlation, or must they be pseudonymized/stripped? You mentioned trace IDs may not be allowed to contain patient identifiers.
3) Confirm required retention window for redacted vs raw logs and whether raw logs may be kept for debugging under stricter controls.
4) KMS policy: should keys be customer-controlled (separate CMK per environment)?

Proposed POC: Redwood will stand up a short sandbox (US region) and run live traffic samples through our audit pipeline with two modes: (A) header/field-level masking (deterministic hashing for non-PII correlation) and (B) strict removal of configured fields. Deliverables: sample redacted log set, config we used, and a short demo showing how to re-run a sanitized trace to reproduce a request.

POC timeline: proposing week of Apr 12 for a 2-3 hour joint session + 1 week of validation.

Attachments: redwood-data-handling-one-pager.pdf (one-pager on our masking/retention defaults).

Next steps (action items):
- Elena: confirm the header list and retention requirements (Q1-Q3 above).
- Tom: confirm who on your infra team should be in the POC and whether we need an MSA/NDA.
- Ben/Marissa: prep the sandbox and POC checklist (Ben, can you include the sample config we discussed?).

Thanks — Mateo

Thanks Mateo — good summary. A few clarifications from our side before we confirm POC dates.

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 3:12 PM Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com> wrote:
> Call highlights (short):
> - Scope: request/response audit stream, request and response bodies, headers, and tracing metadata (trace IDs/span ids).
> - Primary asks: ensure no PHI/sysid/SSN in logs; demonstrate an approach to keep observability for debugging while removing/replacing sensitive values; support US-only residency for logs.

A couple of points:
- Trace IDs: these are currently surface-level artifacts in our tracing pipeline. We can live with trace IDs for debugging only if they are pseudonymized in a way that cannot be linked back to a patient identifier without an authorized process. In practice we need the ability to do a secure, audited re-identification in exceptional cases (not daily).
- Retention: 90 days for redacted audit logs is acceptable. For any raw/unredacted data we require an approval process and will only permit retention for up to 7 days in the sandbox environment.
- Headers: please treat Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, X-User-Email, X-User-Id as sensitive by default. IPs (X-Forwarded-For) must be truncated to /24 or hashed.
- KMS: we require customer-controlled CMK for any persistent storage of audit logs. Ephemeral keys for the sandbox are ok for the POC but must be destroyed after the exercise.

Before the POC we need sample redacted/unredacted log samples to review and a short note on the re-identification workflow (who can trigger it, audit trail).

We can do the POC on Apr 15 at 10:00 AM PT if that works for your team. We will also need a short NDA executed first and an access request form filled out for the sandbox.

Elena

Thanks — jumping in with the technical approach and POC checklist so Acme can validate.

On Apr 3, 2027, at 9:02 AM, Elena Gutierrez <elena.gutierrez@acmehealth.com> wrote:
> - Trace IDs: these are currently surface-level artifacts in our tracing pipeline. We can live with trace IDs for debugging only if they are pseudonymized in a way that cannot be linked back to a patient identifier without an authorized process.

Short answers:
- Trace IDs themselves are just UUIDs; they are not PHI unless they are joined with a user identifier in the same record. Our recommended pattern: 
  1) Field-level scrubber removes any direct PII fields (user_email, ssn, patient_id).
  2) Trace IDs are deterministically hashed with a per-customer salt at ingest for correlation across services. The salt is stored in the customer CMK-wrapped metadata and is accessible only to a restricted support workflow.
  3) For emergency debug, we support a re-identification workflow that requires (a) a Jira ticket (or ticket id in the audit log), (b) two-person approval, and (c) a recorded one-time KMS unwrapping event.

Example config snippet (POC):
- scrubber.rules: [header: Authorization => remove, header: Cookie => remove, header: X-User-Email => mask, body.fields: [patient_id => remove, email => hash]]
- trace.hashing: algorithm: HMAC-SHA256, salt: customer_salt, salt_storage: KMS-encrypted
- retention: redacted_logs: 90d, raw_temp: 7d (ephemeral sandbox only)

Attachments: poc-checklist.xlsx (POC runbook + test vectors). Also linking the draft design doc: https://drive.redwood.com/docs/audit-stream-sanitization-draft

Ben (cc: Mateo, Marissa)
